evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: It ensures the accuracy, consistency, and trustworthiness of product and behavioral data, enabling stakeholders to make informed, data-driven decisions.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities repeatedly emphasize accuracy, consistency, trustworthiness, data validation, and quality checks with no velocity/speed language present, placing this at rigour.
evidence.domain_risk: The position identifies data gaps, validates data integrity, and collaborates with cross-functional teams to improve data pipelines
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Errors affect internal product/behavioral analytics and business decision-making at a global mobility company, a real but non-regulatory, non-financial-reporting consequence, placing this at moderate.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: An existing 'Digital Experience Platform' and Digital Delivery Centres with established analytics and data pipelines are described as being improved and extended, indicating a growing but already-established data function.
evidence.jd_authorship: Hands-on experience supporting event-based measurement implementations using Tag Management Systems or in-product instrumentation.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities name specific technical scope (event-based measurement, Tag Management Systems, in-product instrumentation, data reconciliation across sources) that shows what the role does day to day.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Experience in Product Analytics, Digital Analytics, or a technical Data Analyst role, with exposure to behavioral data.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role centers on product and behavioral analytics (event-based measurement, in-product instrumentation) serving Product/QA/Engineering teams, a product-oriented audience.
evidence.autonomy_level: Own changes end-to-end, including development, testing, deployment, and production validation.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: All responsibilities are scoped execution verbs (design, implement, own changes, build, improve, collaborate, communicate, deliver) responding to defined business/operational requirements rather than setting new strategic direction.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: No AI tooling or AI-adjacent responsibility is mentioned anywhere in the JD.
evidence.testing_framing: Own changes end-to-end, including development, testing, deployment, and production validation.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing and data validation are framed as an owned responsibility with explicit ownership language (own changes end-to-end), not just a tool in a skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: It ensures the accuracy, consistency, and trustworthiness of product and behavioral data, enabling stakeholders to make informed, data-driven decisions.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Data trustworthiness and integrity are named as ongoing secondary concerns without regulatory or stakeholder-trust framing dominating the JD, placing this at moderate.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Continuously improve data assets through incremental enhancements, refactoring, and workflow optimization.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Responsibilities are dominated by improve/refactor/optimize verbs applied to existing data pipelines and analytical assets rather than building new infrastructure from scratch, indicating fix/scale.
evidence.work_arrangement: Flexible Work: Benefit from hybrid or remote work arrangements, with a remote work bonus to recognise your contribution.
evidence.loss_aversion: It ensures the accuracy, consistency, and trustworthiness of product and behavioral data — a secondary data-quality concern, not a dominant compliance risk register.
